questions.prompt: Determine whether the $1.2\text{-kN}$ block shown is in equilibrium and find the magnitude and direction of the friction force when $\theta = 25^\circ$ and $P = 750\,\text{N}$ ($\mu_s = 0.35$, $\mu_k = 0.25$).

options.label: A
options.text: Equilibrium; $F = 172.6\,\text{N}$ down and to the left

options.label: B
options.text: Equilibrium; $F = 172.6\,\text{N}$ up and to the right

options.label: C
options.text: Block moves; $F = 351\,\text{N}$ down and to the left

options.label: D
options.text: Block moves; $F = 492\,\text{N}$ up and to the right

questions.solution:
Resolve forces parallel ($x$ up-left) and perpendicular ($y$) to the $25^\circ$ incline:

$$N = 1200\cos 25^\circ + 750\sin 25^\circ = 1087.6 + 317.0 = 1404.5\,\text{N}$$

$$F_{\text{req}} = P\cos 25^\circ - W\sin 25^\circ = 750\cos 25^\circ - 1200\sin 25^\circ = 679.7 - 507.1 = 172.6\,\text{N}\text{ (down-left)}$$

Maximum static friction is $F_m = \mu_s N = 0.35(1404.5) = 491.6\,\text{N}$. Since $F_{\text{req}} = 172.6\,\text{N} \le 491.6\,\text{N}$, the block remains in equilibrium with $F = 172.6\,\text{N}$ directed down and to the left.

questions.prompt: For the $1.2\text{-kN}$ block shown ($\mu_s = 0.35$, $\mu_k = 0.25$), determine whether the block is in equilibrium and find the friction force when $\theta = 30^\circ$ and $P = 150\,\text{N}$.

options.label: A
options.text: Equilibrium; $F = 470\,\text{N}$ up and to the left

options.label: B
options.text: Block moves; $F = 279\,\text{N}$ up and to the left

options.label: C
options.text: Block moves; $F = 390\,\text{N}$ up and to the left

options.label: D
options.text: Block moves; $F = 279\,\text{N}$ down and to the right

questions.solution:
Compute the normal force and required static friction force:

$$N = 1200\cos 30^\circ + 150\sin 30^\circ = 1039.2 + 75.0 = 1114.2\,\text{N}$$

$$F_{\text{req}} = 1200\sin 30^\circ - 150\cos 30^\circ = 600.0 - 129.9 = 470.1\,\text{N}\text{ (up-left)}$$

Since $F_m = \mu_s N = 0.35(1114.2) = 390.0\,\text{N} < 470.1\,\text{N}$, equilibrium cannot be maintained and the block slides down the incline (to the right). Thus friction is kinetic and directed up and to the left:

$$F_k = \mu_k N = 0.25(1114.2) = 278.6\,\text{N} \approx 279\,\text{N}$$

questions.prompt: Determine whether the $45\text{-lb}$ block on the $30^\circ$ incline is in equilibrium and find the magnitude and direction of the friction force when $P = 100\,\text{lb}$ ($\mu_s = 0.40$, $\mu_k = 0.30$, force $P$ acts at $40^\circ$ to the incline).

options.label: A
options.text: Equilibrium; $F = 54.1\,\text{lb}$ down and to the left

options.label: B
options.text: Block moves; $F = 41.3\,\text{lb}$ down and to the left

options.label: C
options.text: Block moves; $F = 31.0\,\text{lb}$ up and to the right

options.label: D
options.text: Block moves; $F = 31.0\,\text{lb}$ down and to the left

questions.solution:
With $x$ up-left along the $30^\circ$ incline and $y$ normal to it, force $P = 100\,\text{lb}$ acts at $40^\circ$ to the incline (pushing up-left and into the plane):

$$N = 45\cos 30^\circ + 100\sin 40^\circ = 38.97 + 64.28 = 103.25\,\text{lb}$$

$$F_{\text{req}} = 100\cos 40^\circ - 45\sin 30^\circ = 76.60 - 22.50 = 54.10\,\text{lb}\text{ (down-right)}$$

Maximum static friction is $F_m = 0.40(103.25) = 41.30\,\text{lb} < 54.10\,\text{lb}$, so the block slides up-left along the incline. The actual kinetic friction acts opposite to motion (down and to the right):

$$F_k = 0.30(103.25) = 31.0\,\text{lb}$$

questions.prompt: Knowing that the coefficient of static friction between the $25\text{-kg}$ block and the $30^\circ$ incline is $\mu_s = 0.25$, determine the smallest value of $P$ (by optimizing the angle $\beta$) required to start the block moving up the incline.
questions.solution:
The weight is $W = 25(9.81) = 245.25\,\text{N}$ and the static friction angle is $\phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.25) = 14.036^\circ$.

By the law of sines on the force triangle ($\mathbf{W}, \mathbf{P}, \mathbf{R}$):

$$\frac{P}{\sin(30^\circ + \phi_s)} = \frac{W}{\sin(90^\circ - \beta + \phi_s)} = \frac{W}{\cos(\beta - \phi_s)}$$

$P$ is minimized when $\cos(\beta - \phi_s) = 1$, i.e., $\beta = \phi_s = 14.04^\circ$, giving:

$$P_{\min} = 245.25\sin(30^\circ + 14.036^\circ) = 245.25\sin 44.036^\circ = 170.5\,\text{N}$$

questions.prompt: The coefficients of friction between the $500\text{-N}$ block and the $35^\circ$ rail are $\mu_s = 0.30$ and $\mu_k = 0.25$. Knowing that $\theta = 65^\circ$ (measured from the horizontal), determine the smallest value of $P$ required to start the block moving up the rail.
questions.solution:
Resolve forces parallel ($x$ along the $35^\circ$ rail) and normal ($y$) to the rail. The angle between $P$ and the rail is $65^\circ - 35^\circ = 30^\circ$:

$$N = 500\cos 35^\circ - P\sin 30^\circ$$

For impending upward motion, $F_m = 0.30 N$ acts down the rail:

$$P\cos 30^\circ - 500\sin 35^\circ - 0.30(500\cos 35^\circ - P\sin 30^\circ) = 0$$

$$P(\cos 30^\circ + 0.30\sin 30^\circ) = 500(\sin 35^\circ + 0.30\cos 35^\circ)$$

$$P(1.0160) = 409.66 \implies P = 403\,\text{N}$$

questions.prompt: The $20\text{-lb}$ block $A$ and the $30\text{-lb}$ block $B$ are connected by a cable passing over a pulley on an incline of angle $\theta$. Knowing that $\mu_s = 0.15$ between the two blocks and zero between block $B$ and the incline, determine the angle $\theta$ for which motion is impending.
questions.solution:
Since $W_B = 30\,\text{lb} > W_A = 20\,\text{lb}$, impending motion moves $B$ down the incline and $A$ up the incline. Between $A$ and $B$, $N_{AB} = 20\cos\theta$, so $F_{AB} = 0.15(20\cos\theta) = 3\cos\theta$.

- Block $A$ along incline: $T - 20\sin\theta - F_{AB} = 0 \implies T = 20\sin\theta + 3\cos\theta$.
- Block $B$ along incline (frictionless base): $30\sin\theta - T - F_{AB} = 0 \implies T = 30\sin\theta - 3\cos\theta$.

Equating $T$: $10\sin\theta = 6\cos\theta \implies \tan\theta = 0.60 \implies \theta = 31.0^\circ$.

questions.prompt: A $120\text{-lb}$ cabinet is mounted on casters ($24\,\text{in.}$ apart, $\mu_s = 0.30$ when locked). If $h = 32\,\text{in.}$, determine the force $P$ required to move the cabinet to the right when the casters at $B$ are locked and the casters at $A$ are free to rotate.
questions.solution:
When only casters $B$ are locked, $F_A = 0$ and $F_B = 0.30 N_B$, with $P = F_B$ horizontally.

Summing moments about $A$ ($\curvearrowleft + \sum M_A = 0$):

$$N_B(24\,\text{in.}) - 120(12\,\text{in.}) - P(32\,\text{in.}) = 0 \implies N_B = 60 + \frac{4}{3}P$$

Substituting into $P = 0.30 N_B$:

$$P = 0.30\left(60 + \frac{4}{3}P\right) = 18 + 0.4P \implies 0.6P = 18 \implies P = 30.0\,\text{lb}$$

questions.prompt: The $50\text{-lb}$ plate $ABCD$ is attached at $A$ and $D$ to collars that can slide on the vertical rod ($\mu_s = 0.40$ between both collars and the rod). Determine whether the plate is in equilibrium when the vertical upward force applied at $E$ is (a) $P = 0$, and (b) $P = 20\,\text{lb}$.

options.label: A
options.text: (a) Plate in equilibrium; (b) Plate in equilibrium

options.label: B
options.text: (a) Plate moves downward; (b) Plate in equilibrium

options.label: C
options.text: (a) Plate in equilibrium; (b) Plate moves downward

options.label: D
options.text: (a) Plate moves downward; (b) Plate moves downward

questions.solution:
Let $N_A$ act left and $N_D$ act right on the collars. By $\sum F_x = 0$, $N_A = N_D = N$. Taking moments about $D$:

$$N(2\,\text{ft}) - 50(3\,\text{ft}) + P(5\,\text{ft}) = 0 \implies N = 75 - 2.5 P$$

Maximum total vertical friction is $F_m = 2\mu_s N = 0.80(75 - 2.5 P) = 60 - 2P$, while the net downward force to be balanced is $|50 - P|$.

- **(a) $P = 0$:** $F_m = 60\,\text{lb} \ge 50\,\text{lb} \implies$ **Plate in equilibrium**.
- **(b) $P = 20\,\text{lb}$:** $N = 75 - 50 = 25\,\text{lb}$, so $F_m = 0.80(25) = 20\,\text{lb} < 50 - 20 = 30\,\text{lb} \implies$ **Plate moves downward**.

questions.prompt: Two $10^\circ$ wedges of negligible weight are used to move and position a $400\text{-lb}$ block. Knowing that $\mu_s = 0.25$ at all surfaces of contact, determine the smallest horizontal force $P$ that should be applied to the lower wedge as shown.
questions.solution:
The static friction angle is $\phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.25) = 14.036^\circ$.

For the block and upper wedge (total weight $W = 400\,\text{lb}$) moving upward against the right vertical wall, the resultant $R_1$ at the $10^\circ$ interface is inclined at $10^\circ + \phi_s$ to the vertical. Horizontal equilibrium gives $N_w = R_1\sin(10^\circ + \phi_s)$, so downward wall friction is $F_w = \tan\phi_s\,R_1\sin(10^\circ + \phi_s)$. Vertical equilibrium gives:

$$R_1\cos(10^\circ + \phi_s) - \tan\phi_s\,R_1\sin(10^\circ + \phi_s) = W \implies R_1\frac{\cos(10^\circ + 2\phi_s)}{\cos\phi_s} = W$$

For the lower wedge (reactions $R_1$ from above and $R_2$ at $\phi_s$ from the floor):

$$P = R_1\frac{\sin(10^\circ + 2\phi_s)}{\cos\phi_s} = W\tan(10^\circ + 2\phi_s) = 400\tan(38.07^\circ) = 313.3\,\text{lb} \approx 313\,\text{lb}$$

questions.prompt: Wedge $A$ of negligible weight is driven vertically downward between two $100\text{-lb}$ plates $B$ and $C$. The coefficient of static friction between all surfaces of contact is $0.35$. Determine the force $P$ required to start moving the wedge when plates $B$ and $C$ are equally free to move.
questions.solution:
The wedge half-angle from the vertical is $90^\circ - 75^\circ = 15^\circ$, and $\phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.35) = 19.29^\circ$.

On plate $B$, the resultant $R$ from the wedge is inclined at $15^\circ + \phi_s = 34.29^\circ$ below the horizontal. Floor equilibrium for plate $B$ ($W = 100\,\text{lb}$) gives $N_f = 100 + R\sin 34.29^\circ$ and $R\cos 34.29^\circ = \mu_s N_f = 0.35(100 + R\sin 34.29^\circ)$, whence $R = 55.62\,\text{lb}$.

By symmetry on wedge $A$: $P = 2R\sin(15^\circ + \phi_s) = 2(55.62)\sin 34.29^\circ = 62.7\,\text{lb}$.

questions.prompt: A high-strength structural bolt has a required bolt tension of $210\,\text{kN}$, thread mean diameter $22.6\,\text{mm}$, and lead $3\,\text{mm}$ (square-threaded). Assuming $\mu_s = 0.40$ on the threads and neglecting washer friction, determine the required tightening couple.
questions.solution:
Mean radius is $r = 11.3\,\text{mm} = 0.0113\,\text{m}$. Compute the lead angle $\theta$ and friction angle $\phi_s$:

$$\tan\theta = \frac{L}{2\pi r} = \frac{3\,\text{mm}}{\pi(22.6\,\text{mm})} = 0.04225 \implies \theta = 2.419^\circ$$

$$\phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.40) = 21.801^\circ$$

Tightening couple:

$$M = W r \tan(\theta + \phi_s) = (210\times 10^3\,\text{N})(0.0113\,\text{m})\tan(24.221^\circ) = 1068\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$$

questions.prompt: The ends of fixed rods $A$ (right-hand thread) and $B$ (left-hand thread) each have a single-threaded screw of mean radius $6\,\text{mm}$ and pitch $2\,\text{mm}$, with $\mu_s = 0.12$. Determine the couple that must be applied to the sleeve to draw the rods closer together under $2\text{-kN}$ tension.
questions.solution:
Because both ends advance simultaneously as the sleeve turns, the total torque is the sum of the tightening torques at $A$ and $B$ ($2 \times Wr\tan(\theta + \phi_s)$):

$$\tan\theta = \frac{2\,\text{mm}}{2\pi(6\,\text{mm})} = 0.05305 \implies \theta = 3.037^\circ, \qquad \phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.12) = 6.843^\circ$$

$$M = 2(2000\,\text{N})(0.006\,\text{m})\tan(3.037^\circ + 6.843^\circ) = 24\tan(9.880^\circ) = 4.18\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$$

questions.prompt: The double pulley shown ($90\text{-mm}$ outer radius carrying the $20\text{-kg}$ mass, $45\text{-mm}$ inner radius carrying downward force $P$) is attached to a $10\text{-mm}$-radius shaft that fits loosely in a fixed bearing ($\mu_s = 0.40$). Determine the force $P$ required to start raising the load.
questions.solution:
Load weight is $W = 20(9.81) = 196.2\,\text{N}$. Using the small-angle approximation for the circle of friction:

$$r_f \approx r\mu_s = (10\,\text{mm})(0.40) = 4.0\,\text{mm}$$

To start raising the $20\text{-kg}$ mass (clockwise impending rotation), the bearing contact shifts $4.0\,\text{mm}$ to the right of center $O$. Summing moments about the line of action of $\mathbf{R}$:

$$196.2(90 + 4.0) - P(45 - 4.0) = 0 \implies P = \frac{196.2 \times 94}{41} = 450\,\text{N}$$

questions.prompt: A $50\text{-lb}$ electric floor polisher ($18\text{-in.}$ disk diameter) is operated on a surface for which $\mu_k = 0.25$. Assuming uniform pressure between the disk and floor, determine the magnitude $Q$ of the horizontal couple forces ($20\,\text{in.}$ apart) required to prevent motion of the machine.
questions.solution:
Using Eq. (8.9) for disk friction over a full circular area of radius $R = 9\,\text{in.}$:

$$M = \frac{2}{3}\mu_k P R = \frac{2}{3}(0.25)(50\,\text{lb})(9\,\text{in.}) = 75.0\,\text{lb}\cdot\text{in.}$$

This frictional torque is balanced by the handle couple $Q(20\,\text{in.})$:

$$Q = \frac{75.0\,\text{lb}\cdot\text{in.}}{20\,\text{in.}} = 3.75\,\text{lb}$$

questions.prompt: Determine the horizontal force required to move a $2500\text{-lb}$ automobile with $23\text{-in.}$-diameter tires along a horizontal road at constant speed, neglecting all friction except rolling resistance with $b = 0.05\,\text{in.}$
questions.solution:
Tire radius is $r = \frac{23\,\text{in.}}{2} = 11.5\,\text{in.}$ Applying Eq. (8.10) ($Pr = Wb$):

$$P = \frac{Wb}{r} = \frac{(2500\,\text{lb})(0.05\,\text{in.})}{11.5\,\text{in.}} = 10.87\,\text{lb}$$

questions.prompt: A band brake controls a $360\text{-mm}$-radius flywheel rotating counterclockwise at constant speed ($\mu_s = 0.30, \mu_k = 0.25$). Determine the magnitude of the couple applied to the flywheel when $P = 45\,\text{N}$.
questions.solution:
Sum moments about hinge $C$ on lever $ABC$:

$$T_B(120\,\text{mm}) - 45(360 + 120)\,\text{mm} = 0 \implies T_B = 45 \times 4 = 180\,\text{N}$$

As the drum turns counterclockwise, friction pulls the band from the lower-left fixed anchor ($T_1$) clockwise around $\beta = 270^\circ = \frac{3\pi}{2}\,\text{rad}$ toward $B$ ($T_2 = 180\,\text{N}$). Since the drum is slipping, use $\mu_k = 0.25$:

$$T_1 = \frac{T_2}{e^{\mu_k \beta}} = \frac{180}{e^{0.25(3\pi/2)}} = \frac{180}{3.248} = 55.42\,\text{N}$$

Resisting couple on the flywheel:

$$M = (T_2 - T_1)r = (180 - 55.42)(0.360\,\text{m}) = 44.9\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$$
